text: Traditional finance is moving onto crypto rails. Perpetuals on stocks, gold and oil grew into a large part of perp trading on major venues while $BTC sat in a bear market. Our new report with Fasanara Digital examines what that means for allocators.

$BTC is testing the ETF cost basis around $81K again. The same level capped the May rally before a deep drop, and caught last week's sweep from just below. A convincing close below it would put mid $70K levels back into play.

BTC treasury companies are in profit but barely buying. They hold $BTC at a cost basis of about $80K, and price has closed above it since September 18. In profit, buying can feed on itself: purchases lift price, price lifts their shares, and their shares fund more purchases.

$BTC is boxed in between $80K and $87K. Below, buyers refilled the bids at the ETF and treasury cost basis. Above, the top buyers' break-even, the main asks and the largest liquidation clusters share one zone. More on ETF flows, MSCI and altcoins in this week's Week On-chain.

Binance asks and the biggest liquidation clusters sit around $87K. The top buyers still cap $BTC price near the same levels. A daily close above that level with ETF inflows would show buyers absorbing the supply. More in this week's Week On Chain

The Q4 levels for $BTC have held so far. Last month, together with @colin_basco and the @CoinbaseInsto team we put resistance at $87K to $87.8K in our Charting Crypto report. We read the data as near-term consolidation. Price stalled there and ranged below it ever since. A break out of the range is likely to spark significant volatility, although another overhead supply cluster sits around $90k. Read our full quarterly report below 👇 https://twitter.com/glassnode/status/2110737242608246947

ETF buyers came back in size yesterday. US spot $BTC ETFs took in $663M, the most in a day since September, and all of it went into BlackRock's IBIT. That single day erased the funds' net outflows for October. Follow-through would confirm the demand is back.
